decisions.reason: F4 and Proof 3.1 require a nonempty inversion set to apply the negative-height geometric inverse. The two cited interfaces prove the rho-difference sum and define word length but do not prove nonemptiness. Added the existing, directly checked strong-exchange lemma: |Inv(w^-1)|=ell(w^-1)>0 for w!=1, since a zero-letter word is the identity; F2 then makes the sum nonzero.

F4 and Verification 3.1 omit the actual-weight hypothesis in the termination corollary. At the nonweight mu=-3theta, mu+rho=-2theta gives D(mu)=0; in the theta-string, the j=2 and j=4 contributions have pairings -||theta||^2 and +||theta||^2 and cancel, so Freudenthal reads 0=0 there too. The Example already restricts its conclusion to the six actual extremal weights, and m_theta(0)=2 is correct; qualifying F4 and step 3.1 repairs the overstatement without changing that claim.

reviews.reason: Reviewed the cone-ring convolution, additive integer height, rho-difference identity, finite alternant and the complete strong-exchange proof. Each fixed coefficient of the inverse has finitely many powers and convolution terms; cancellation yields one. The new F4 supplies nonzero rho-wrho for every nonidentity w, validating part (iv), including the empty-root case. No AC or denominator identity is needed; Statement unchanged.

Checked the full termination corollary, shifted-norm proof and actual adjoint weight list, together with the Freudenthal formula and extremal-weight supplier. At zero D=3||theta||^2, only j=1 at each positive root contributes, and the right side is 6||theta||^2, giving multiplicity two. Strict positivity at every actual non-top weight justifies the repaired qualified F4 and step 3.1; it does not imply uniqueness for nonweights. AC remains explicit and the Example is unchanged.
